(Today through Tuesday)...
Issued at 133 AM EDT Wed Oct 7 2026

Today Through Thursday.

Surface high pressure centered along the Mid-Atlantic coast and 
broad mid-level ridging positioned over the eastern third of the 
CONUS will maintain southwesterly low-level flow across the Ohio 
Valley through Wednesday. Deep-layer subsidence and low column 
moisture will keep skies mostly clear. Boundary-layer mixing under 
full insolation will easily allow afternoon temperatures to warm 
into the upper 70s, roughly 8 to 10 degrees above normal. HREF 
ensemble member soundings show strong daytime momentum transfer 
within the mixed layer, yielding southwesterly surface winds of 10 
to 12 mph with occasional gusts up to 18 to 20 mph Wednesday 
afternoon. This strong mixing will also help to bring lower 
afternoon dewpoints with min RH values below 40 percent, and locally 
lower than 30 percent with models often underdoing the afternoon 
dewpoint drop in this pattern. Lows Wednesday night will drop into 
the lower 50s under clear skies and light south-southwesterly flow.

On Thursday, a northern stream shortwave trough tracking across the 
Upper Great Lakes will push a weak, moisture-starved surface trough 
south across central Indiana. GFS and ECMWF soundings show a 
persistent layer of dry air in the 850mb to 500mb layer, with 
forcing for ascent remaining well north of the forecast area. 
Consequently, the boundary will pass dry with PoPs held under 10%. 
Winds will veer to the northwest around 10 mph behind the boundary. 
Minor cold air advection will be largely offset by continued 
insolation, keeping afternoon high temperatures more towards the 
upper 70s. High pressure building in from the Upper Midwest Thursday 
night will allow for efficient radiational cooling, dropping 
overnight lows into the mid to upper 40s.

Friday Through Tuesday.

Surface high pressure translates eastward across the Great Lakes on 
Friday, maintaining dry conditions and light east to southeast 
surface flow across central Indiana. High temperatures will remain 
mild in the mid 70s under mostly sunny skies, with overnight lows 
Friday night slightly milder with stronger surface winds helping to 
keep radiational cooling less efficient.

The primary focus of the extended period continues to be the 
potential for tropical moisture impacts over the weekend. A mid-
level trough over the Central Plains is forecast to interact with 
tropical moisture associated with Tropical Depression Nine moving 
north out of the Gulf states. Ensemble and deterministic guidance 
from the GFS, ECMWF, GEFS, and EPS display strong consensus in 
developing a broad poleward moisture transport corridor streaming 
northeastward into the Ohio Valley. Mid-level cloud cover will 
increase through the day Saturday with high temperatures topping out 
in the mid 70s. Strong isentropic ascent, coupled with upper-level 
divergence in the right-rear quadrant of an accelerating jet streak 
over the Great Lakes, will generate rain across the region beginning 
late Saturday night through Sunday morning with the main uncertainty 
being exactly where the tropical remnants will track. NBM and EPS 
probabilities for 24-hour rainfall exceeding 0.50 inches remain in 
the 60 to 70 percent range for central and southern portions of the 
forecast area. Persistent cloudiness and precipitation will hold 
daytime highs to the upper 60s on Sunday, with lows remaining 
elevated in the upper 50s.

Rain will taper off late Sunday afternoon into Sunday night as the 
tropical moisture plume shifts east toward the Appalachian region 
and the primary trough axis translates east. Subtropical ridging and 
a broad mid-level dry slot build back over the region on Monday, 
leading to quick clearing and rebound warming. High temperatures on 
Monday will climb back into the upper 70s to near 80 under return 
southwesterly flow. By Tuesday, a secondary northern stream 
shortwave and associated surface cold front will sweep through the 
Midwest. Strong cold air advection behind the front will bring 
cooler weather towards mid-week.
